messages:
carlos: Heads up — in prod I'm seeing traces where the root span exists but most child spans vanish after a KV cache refill spike around 21:03. Any quick troubleshooting pointers? Example trace: https://observability.internal/traces/trace-abc123

anya: Which service and a trace id would help — prefetcher, batcher, or consumer?

carlos: Prefetcher-v2, trace id is trace-abc123 (link above). Pattern: request enters, root + a couple internal spans show, then no DB write / consumer spans. Logs show the HTTP hit and then the message put on kafka, but the consumer doesn't seem to attach spans.

lee: Quick checks: 1) are we still using tracecontext propagator end-to-end? 2) did we change the propagator ordering in last night's deploy?

carlos: We already use tracecontext. Agent is opentelemetry-javaagent 1.20.0 and start args include: `-javaagent:/opt/otel/agent.jar -Dotel.resource.attributes=service.name=prefetcher-v2`

mike: If root is present and downstream is missing, sampling fallthrough at the worker side is common. What's the sampling config on the consumer/worker?

anya: Also check kafka client header passthrough — older kafka-clients versions we had stripped unknown headers that carried traceparent. We recently bumped clients in a different service; maybe this one missed it. Internal note: kafka-clients 3.5.0 retains headers consistently.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy of prefetcher-v2 completed at 2025-07-19T21:10Z :white_check_mark:

lee: Try a short repro: set the consumer to OTEL_SAMPLER=always_on and OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp for ~5-10 minutes to confirm whether spans are being created but dropped by sampling. Also validate OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext,baggage explicitly on both sides.

carlos: I'll flip always_on for the consumer for 10m and watch. Any quick dashboards/metrics to watch while I do that?

anya: Dashboards: traces overview: https://observability.internal/dash/traces-overview and span coverage: https://observability.internal/dash/span-coverage. Metric to watch: `env.metrics.kafka.header.drop.rate` and our `trace.handoff.success.rate` (span coverage panel).

mike: Helpful log grep: search for traceparent headers on both producer and consumer logs: `grep traceparent /var/log/prefetcher/*.log` and on consumer: `grep traceparent /var/log/consumer/*.log`. If header present in producer and absent in consumer, it's header passthrough issue.

carlos: Running the consumer with always_on now. Will post results in ~10m. Thanks for the checklist :pray: 

lee: If that shows children appear with always_on, we'll add a short-lived sampling rule to keep handoffs from gateway->worker always_on and then follow up with a proper sampling rollout.

carlos: Update: after 8m with always_on I see downstream spans reappear in the trace viewer for trace-abc123 and others. Looks like header propagation got lost intermittently. I'll open a follow-up PR to upgrade kafka-clients and add a test for header passthrough.

anya: Nice, thanks. If you can include the grep output and the offsets of affected messages in the PR that'll speed the fix.

carlos: Will attach logs + trace links in the PR. Closing this check-in — will ping when PR is up.
